stem: During a school science exhibition in Jaipur, Meena displays four samples she collected at home: an Amoeba seen in pond water, bread mould grown on a stale roti, a culture of bacteria from curd, and a virus sample studied from a chart. Her teacher asks her to label each sample correctly. Which row of her chart is correct?

options.text: Amoeba – protozoan; bread mould – fungus; bacteria – bacterium; virus – multiplies only inside living cells
Amoeba – bacterium; bread mould – protozoan; bacteria – fungus; virus – an alga
Amoeba – protozoan; bread mould – bacterium; bacteria – fungus; virus – multiplies outside living cells
All four samples are bacteria because they are all microscopic

teacher.key_rationale: Amoeba is a protozoan, bread mould (Rhizopus) is a fungus, bacteria from curd are bacteria, and viruses are acellular and multiply only inside living cells, so row A is fully correct. Rows B and C misclassify the groups; option D captures the misconception that anything microscopic is a bacterium and that viruses multiply outside cells.
